basis: Infection-associated inflammation of the umbilical cord; the supplied definition establishes leukocyte migration, without establishing vascular injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: leukocyte migration from umbilical vessels does not itself establish vasculitis or vascular damage.

basis: Cytopenic immunodeficiency; hearing loss 80-99% and optic abnormalities/visual loss 30-79%. Respiratory failure lacks evidence of direct intrinsic pulmonary damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory failure is annotated 80-99%, but intrinsic lung injury is not established; recurrent infections are separately diagnosed complications.
decisions.ocular: involved: optic nerve abnormalities with visual loss are annotated frequent (30-79%), supporting structural and functional eye involvement.

basis: Defining congenital skin creases; intellectual disability 4/4 and callosal hypoplasia 2/2; microphthalmia 4/4; cleft palate 3/4. Ureterocele 1/4 excluded.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability 4/4 and callosal hypoplasia 2/2 establish common neurodevelopmental involvement accompanying the defining skin disorder.
decisions.ocular: involved: microphthalmia in 4/4 establishes common structural eye involvement accompanying the defining skin disorder.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia with calcium/phosphate disorder; ptosis 6/6 and hearing loss 3/5. Dental abnormalities omitted by cap; nephrocalcinosis 5-29% excluded.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: delayed tooth eruption 3/3 and malocclusion 3/5 support involvement, but dental findings are omitted under the four-axis cap.
decisions.ocular: involved: persistent ptosis in 6/6 represents eyelid dysfunction; its frequency supports retention under the four-axis cap.

basis: Organic aciduria defined by progressive neurodegeneration; strabismus and vertebral abnormalities each occur in 30-79%. A single cardiac report does not establish common involvement.

decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus is annotated frequent (30-79%) and represents persistent impairment of ocular alignment and binocular function.

basis: Facial dermal melanocytosis; scleral pigmentation in about two-thirds does not itself impair ocular function. Glaucoma and uveal melanoma are separate disease risks.

decisions.ocular: none: scleral pigmentation (~67%) does not establish functional damage; glaucoma and uveal melanoma are separate later disease risks.

basis: Autoinflammatory panniculitis; inflammatory joint swelling 3/3 and vasculitis 1/3 (~33%) support involvement. Diarrhea 3/3 alone does not establish intestinal injury.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: vasculitis directly injures vessels and is reported in 1/3 (~33%); this meets the threshold, with substantial small-series uncertainty.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: diarrhea 3/3 and chronic diarrhea 1/3 establish symptoms, but the supplied evidence does not establish direct inflammatory or structural bowel injury.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment, deafness and osteodystrophy define DOORS; nail hypoplasia ~100% retained as involved under the primary cap. Gingival overgrowth 3/3 omitted by total cap.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: diagnostic nail hypoplasia occurs in essentially 100%; retained here because the three primary slots prioritize neurologic, hearing and skeletal disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: osteodystrophy defines DOORS, with short distal finger phalanges in 30/30; skeletal involvement is a core diagnostic component.

basis: Named syndrome indicates ear and skeletal abnormalities; no definition or phenotypes establish endocrine dysfunction from the gonadal component.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: gonadal abnormalities alone do not establish hormonal dysfunction; reproductive structural disease has no axis, and confirming endocrine evidence is absent.

basis: Lysosomal storage disease with characteristic intrinsic immunodeficiency; cognitive and hearing impairment are common (>30%). Major skeletal abnormalities are generally absent in mild type 1.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: intrinsic immune dysfunction is a characteristic component of alpha-mannosidosis, including the mild phenotype; this is more than susceptibility to a separate infection.
